raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A storage backend learns its host pools from a burst of hooks: the anchor pool through `register_mem_pool_host`, then every pool of the host pool group through `register_mem_host_pool_v2` — but nothing told the backend when the burst was over. A backend that must finalize once the pool set is known (e.g. register the instance with a remote cache manager whose spec cannot be amended after registration) had no correct moment to act and could only defer that work to the first data-path call, paying seconds of setup on the first request and surfacing config errors (manager unreachable, instance conflict) after startup instead of failing it.

## Modifications

- `HiCacheStorage` gains a no-op `on_host_pools_registered()`: fires exactly once per attach, right after the last call of the initial burst; pools registered later (dynamic draft sidecars) arrive through v2 alone and do not re-fire it. Raising fails the attach.
- The burst ends in different places on the two controllers, so each fires the hook at its own end: the base controller right after the anchor pool, `HybridCacheController` — whose per-pool v2 loop runs after `super().attach_storage_backend()` returns — after that loop. A `_registers_host_pools_after_super_attach` flag tells the two apart; no signatures change and no code moves.
- The hook defaults to a no-op, so existing backends are unaffected.
- Documents the registration lifecycle in `hicache_design.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no model output changes). New CPU unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py`: the hybrid hook fires after its v2 burst exactly once, the base hook fires right after the anchor pool, base-path hook failure rolls the attach back, hybrid-path failure propagates, dynamic sidecars do not re-fire the hook.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

The simulator failure was the simulator's own `MockHiCacheStorage`: it is duck-typed (hijacks `StorageBackendFactory.create_backend`) and did not inherit the new hook's no-op default. Fixed in c3fd4dc4 by adding the no-op; `simulator-test-cpu` passes on the latest run.

The remaining failures do not touch this change (`on_host_pools_registered` appears in none of their stacks):

- `base-b-test-1-npu-a3` / `base-b-test-2-npu-a3`: NPU host-memory OOM (`aclrtMallocHostWithCfg` error 207001) while allocating the 30 GB host pool, with `hicache_storage_backend: None` -- no backend, so the hook is never called. The second one fails in an RL indexer-replay test instead.
- `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd`: EAGLE spec test with `enable_hierarchical_cache: False`; server watchdog timeout on ROCm.
- `build-test` spr2: `test_crash_dump.py` server crash cascading into connection-refused failures, plus `test_subblock_sparse_attention.py` raising "Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled" on the CPU runner. The other partitions were cancelled as cascade.

Follow-up: rebased onto latest main (2f3e02c5) and fixed the PR title to the required format — the previous title failed the title gate at 09:42, whose fast-fail then cancelled the in-flight jobs of that run (that is what most of the red checks on that run are: cancelled cascades, not test failures). @@ -162,6 +162,8 @@ SGLang supports a PD (Prefill-Decode) disaggregation deployment mode through the
 
 HiCache encapsulates all read, write, and query operations on L3 backends within the `class HiCacheStorage(ABC)`, exposing a set of simple and consistent interfaces. This design supports a wide range of L3 storage backends and allows users to select the one that best fits their specific use cases.
 
+When a backend is attached, HiCache hands it the host memory pools in a fixed order: `register_mem_pool_host` receives the anchor pool first, then every pool of the host pool group (Mamba state, indexer, SWA, draft sidecars, ...) arrives through `register_mem_host_pool_v2`, and `on_host_pools_registered` fires exactly once when this initial burst is over. Pools attached dynamically later still arrive through `register_mem_host_pool_v2` alone. Backends that talk to an external service whose instance specification must be complete up front (e.g. a remote cache manager) should finalize it inside `on_host_pools_registered`; raising there fails the attach.
+
 - **Mooncake**: Mooncake is a high-performance caching system for LLM inference that leverages RDMA and multi-NIC resources to enable zero-copy, ultra-fast data transfers. Try Mooncake [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store).
 
 - **DeepSeek 3FS (HF3FS)**: HF3FS is a Kubernetes-native distributed storage solution with operator-based deployment. Try HF3FS [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/hf3fs).

+# ==============================================================================
+"""The storage backend's view of the initial host-pool registration burst.
+
+``on_host_pools_registered`` fires exactly once per attach, immediately after
+the last call of the initial burst: the anchor pool on the base controller
+(its whole burst), after the per-pool v2 loop on the hybrid controller (which
+continues the burst after super() returns). Pools registered later (dynamic
+sidecars) arrive through v2 alone and do not re-fire the hook.
+
+    python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py -v
+"""
+
+import threading
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any, List, Optional
+from unittest import mock
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.cache_controller import HiCacheController
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import PoolName
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hybrid_cache.hybrid_cache_controller import (
+    HybridCacheController,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host import HostPoolGroup, PoolEntry
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.storage import StorageBackendFactory
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+PAGE = 16
+
+
+class RecordingBackend:
+    """A backend that records the registration calls it receives."""
+
+    def __init__(self, order: List[str], fail_on_complete: bool = False):
+        self.order = order
+        self.fail_on_complete = fail_on_complete
+        self.closed = False
+
+    def register_mem_pool_host(self, mem_pool_host: Any) -> None:
+        self.order.append("v1")
+
+    def register_mem_host_pool_v2(self, host_pool: Any, host_pool_name: Any) -> None:
+        self.order.append(f"v2:{host_pool_name}")
+
+    def on_host_pools_registered(self) -> None:
+        self.order.append("complete")
+        if self.fail_on_complete:
+            raise RuntimeError("registration failed in the backend")
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.closed = True
+
+
+def _fake_pool(name: str) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    """The HostPoolGroup surface, without CUDA."""
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        name=name,
+        layout="page_first",
+        page_size=PAGE,
+        device="cpu",
+        size=128,
+        logical_size=128,
+        can_use_write_back_jit=True,
+    )
+
+
+def _entry(name: PoolName, pool: Any, is_anchor: bool = False) -> PoolEntry:
+    return PoolEntry(
+        name=name,
+        host_pool=pool,
+        device_pool=SimpleNamespace(),
+        layer_mapper=lambda layer: layer,
+        is_primary_index_anchor=is_anchor,
+    )
+
+
+def _group() -> HostPoolGroup:
+    return HostPoolGroup(
+        [
+            _entry(PoolName.KV, _fake_pool("kv"), is_anchor=True),
+            _entry(PoolName.MAMBA, _fake_pool("mamba")),
+        ]
+    )
+
+
+def _controller(cls: type, storage_host_pool: Any, mem_pool_host: Any) -> Any:
+    """Only the attributes ``attach_storage_backend`` reads."""
+    controller = object.__new__(cls)
+    controller.enable_storage = False
+    controller.storage_stop_event = threading.Event()
+    controller.storage_host_pool = storage_host_pool
+    controller.mem_pool_host = mem_pool_host
+    controller.page_size = PAGE
+    controller.host_memory_mode = "cache"
+    controller.tp_group = None
+    controller.attn_cp_group = None
+    controller.attn_tp_group = None
+    controller.pp_group = None
+    controller.prefetch_hits_sync_groups = []
+    controller.prefetch_completion_sync_groups = []
+    if cls is HybridCacheController:
+        controller.pp_prefetch_command_thread = None
+        controller.pp_prefetch_command_group = None
+        controller.extra_host_mem_release_queues = {}
+    return controller
+
+
+def _attach(
+    controller: Any,
+    backend: RecordingBackend,
+    order: List[str],
+    host_pools: Optional[List[PoolEntry]] = None,
+) -> None:
+    """Run ``attach_storage_backend`` with the heavy pieces stubbed out."""
+    storage_config = SimpleNamespace(is_mla_model=False, extra_config={})
+    # Only the hybrid attach accepts host_pools; the base attach's burst is
+    # the anchor pool alone.
+    kwargs = {"host_pools": host_pools} if host_pools is not None else {}
+    with (
+        mock.patch.object(
+            StorageBackendFactory, "create_backend", return_value=backend
+        ),
+        mock.patch.object(
+            controller, "_generate_storage_config", return_value=storage_config
+        ),
+        mock.patch.object(
+            controller,
+            "_start_storage_threads",
+            side_effect=lambda: order.append("threads"),
+        ),
+    ):
+        controller.attach_storage_backend(storage_backend="dynamic", **kwargs)
+
+
+class TestRegistrationBurstOrder(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_hybrid_hook_fires_after_its_v2_burst(self):
+        # super() completes (threads included, as before), then the hybrid
+        # burst continues and the hook fires at its end -- once.
+        order: List[str] = []
+        group = _group()
+        controller = _controller(
+            HybridCacheController, group.anchor_entry.host_pool, group
+        )
+
+        _attach(controller, RecordingBackend(order), order, host_pools=group.entries)
+
+        self.assertEqual(order, ["v1", "threads", "v2:kv", "v2:mamba", "complete"])
+
+    def test_base_hook_fires_right_after_the_anchor_pool(self):
+        # Without a host pool group the burst is the anchor pool alone, so
+        # the hook fires inside the base attach.
+        order: List[str] = []
+        pool = _fake_pool("kv")
+        controller = _controller(HiCacheController, pool, pool)
+
+        _attach(controller, RecordingBackend(order), order)
+
+        self.assertEqual(order, ["v1", "complete", "threads"])
+
+    def test_base_hook_failure_rolls_the_attach_back(self):
+        # On the base path the hook runs inside the attach's guarded section,
+        # so a backend failure rolls the backend back through the existing
+        # error path.
+        order: List[str] = []
+        pool = _fake_pool("kv")
+        controller = _controller(HiCacheController, pool, pool)
+        backend = RecordingBackend(order, fail_on_complete=True)
+

issue_comments.body:
The simulator failure was the simulator's own `MockHiCacheStorage`: it is duck-typed (hijacks `StorageBackendFactory.create_backend`) and did not inherit the new hook's no-op default. Fixed in c3fd4dc4 by adding the no-op; `simulator-test-cpu` passes on the latest run.

The remaining failures do not touch this change (`on_host_pools_registered` appears in none of their stacks):

- `base-b-test-1-npu-a3` / `base-b-test-2-npu-a3`: NPU host-memory OOM (`aclrtMallocHostWithCfg` error 207001) while allocating the 30 GB host pool, with `hicache_storage_backend: None` -- no backend, so the hook is never called. The second one fails in an RL indexer-replay test instead.
- `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd`: EAGLE spec test with `enable_hierarchical_cache: False`; server watchdog timeout on ROCm.
- `build-test` spr2: `test_crash_dump.py` server crash cascading into connection-refused failures, plus `test_subblock_sparse_attention.py` raising "Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled" on the CPU runner. The other partitions were cancelled as cascade.

Follow-up: rebased onto latest main (2f3e02c5) and fixed the PR title to the required format — the previous title failed the title gate at 09:42, whose fast-fail then cancelled the in-flight jobs of that run (that is what most of the red checks on that run are: cancelled cascades, not test failures). The title check and lint now pass on the latest run.

The rebase itself is conflict-free and the hook semantics are unchanged. Could you re-trigger the cancelled suites (e.g. `/rerun-failed-ci`) when convenient? I don't have permission to rerun them from a fork.

The branch itself is ready: rebased on latest main, title fixed, lint + title check pass.
